title: A fix names a game part and is applied in the class
text: A porting rule is text: a pattern on the compiler's error and a find-and-replace on the source (355 of 358 rules), so it cannot reach a .jar and cannot tell LocalPlayer.sendSystemMessage from ServerPlayer.sendSystemMessage. A rule names the game member it replaces and what replaces it (a call, a call chain, a field read through a method), and JarPort applies it where a class references that member; a source port applies the same rule at the places the compiler resolved. A rule's test links its before against the old release and its after against the new one, in seconds, with no mod. The jar scoreboard's top entries are the order: GuiGraphics.blit (52 mods), RenderSystem.setShader (43), InteractionResult's fields (28), Registry.getTag (29).
finish: 50 of the 150 most-downloaded NeoForge mods for 1.21.1 link against 1.21.2 (32 today), and every one that needs no other mod loads on a real 1.21.2 server
wrongIf: the link count rises and python bench/exposure.py load does not
result: So far (2026-11-18): JarPort applies in the class what the game's own code shows (calls switched, added arguments such as GuiGraphics.blit's RenderType::guiTextured, chains, narrower fields) and every port rule's inClass: a Java expression for the old member, compiled against the new release like javac would, or a dropped class mapped to its replacement. 57 replacements on 33 rules. 41 of 150 link (30 before), broken uses 5,640 -> 4,147; on a real 1.21.2 server 30 of 35 load and all 19 that link load. The rest are held back by 1.21.2's rendering and recipe rewrites (render states, toasts, recipe book), which one-member replacements cannot express: every remaining mixin signature change would add about 4. Next: the source port applies inClass too. Source ports (2026-11-21, PR: source answers): mmt port --fix plans, on the sources as written and against the mod's own compile, every use of a member the new release no longer has as declared, and writes the same answer a jar port writes there (the route map's learned replacements and the rules' inClass, chosen and checked against the new release by JarPort itself, tools/SourceAnswers.java), after the preflight; an answer the new release's compiler rejects is put back. On the 129-port sweep (cloud runs 44950219786 vs main 44950233600): 13 ports end with fewer errors, none with more from it, errors left on ports both runs measured 4,610 -> 4,504; builds stay 15. ZombieApocalypseAddon 1.21.1 -> 26.3 builds with 49 answers written and loads on a real 26.3 server and client. Next: the learner's coverage of what the source ports still lack (the sweep's semantic-api-change class, 2,442 errors).
